cues.text: Section thirteen: Archived examination practice.
In this section, only questions that directly assess Session 5 performance and recovery concepts are included.
The original numbering and options are retained.
Please note that the suggested answers are tutor reasoning, not official marking keys.
Questions that ask mainly about general management functions or infrastructure challenges are excluded, even when their scenarios mention recovery.
We begin with the pre-test questions.
Pre-test Question 6.
An IT dashboard displays a spike in page load time during a product launch.
The KPI that best reflects this decline in performance is blank.
Option a: CSAT, which stands for Customer Satisfaction.
Option b: response time.
Option c: MTBF.
Option d: FCR, which stands for First Contact Resolution.
The suggested answer is b.
Response time directly tracks latency and performance degradation.
A spike in page load time is exactly a latency problem, and response time is the indicator that measures it.
Next, Pre-test Question 9.
A healthcare organisation decides to maintain a warm site for disaster recovery.
This decision balances cost and speed by blank.
Option a: pre-configuring infrastructure without full replication.
Option b: relying solely on weekly manual backups.
Option c: using staff volunteers for testing.
Option d: automating firewall rule changes.
The suggested answer is a.
Warm sites have infrastructure prepared for recovery, but are usually less ready than fully replicated hot sites.
That is the balance: some preparation to speed recovery, without the full cost of complete replication.
Now we move to the CA questions.
Remember that CA means continuous assessment.
CA Question 19.
After cloud cost overruns affected operational budgets at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited, governance teams introduced dashboards tracking system uptime, customer complaints, and deployment delays.
Which principle is being implemented MOST directly?
Option A: Performance measurement through Key Performance Indicators, or KPIs, analysis.
Option B: Resource optimisation through hybrid workforce restructuring initiatives.
Option C: Infrastructure governance through centralised database administration controls.
Option D: Strategic alignment through enterprise digital transformation initiatives.
The suggested answer is A.
Uptime, complaints and deployment delays are measurable indicators used to evaluate operational performance.
Finally, CA Question 29.
After cloud cost overruns affected operational budgets at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited, governance teams introduced dashboards tracking system uptime, customer complaints, and deployment delays.
Which principle is being implemented MOST directly?
Option A: Infrastructure governance through centralised database administration controls.
Option B: Strategic alignment through enterprise digital transformation initiatives.
Option C: Performance measurement through Key Performance Indicators, or KPIs, analysis.
Option D: Resource optimisation through hybrid workforce restructuring initiatives.
The suggested answer is C.
This repeats Question 19 with shuffled options.
KPI analysis measures performance against objectives.
That completes the archived examination practice for this session.
